  "consensus_summary": "Primary consensus identifies justification as God's forensic declaration that a sinner is righteous before Him (classically via imputation of Christ's righteousness), received by faith apart from works; alternatives include transformative infusion, covenantal membership, and demonstrative vindication by works.",
  "book_summary": "To judge, declare, or demonstrate a person, word, deed, or cause right against a question or charge (opposite of condemn); God answers the charge against the sinner by grace through Christ, forgiving rather than renaming ungodliness righteousness; deeds may vindicate claimed faith but cannot purchase mercy or place God in debt.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "forensic declaration that the sinner is righteous by faith through Christ",
  "book_core_identification": "declaration or demonstration of rightness against a charge; for the sinner, God's gracious forgiveness through Christ rather than renaming ungodliness righteousness",
  "core_relation": "COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP",
  "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Book elevates general judicial and demonstrative uses (persons, words, deeds, causes, wisdom, God himself) to the primary definition rather than secondary alternatives; for the soteriological case it recharacterizes the declaration as forgiveness/non-imputation of sin while excluding or polemically rejecting 'renaming ungodliness righteousness' (imputation language), and insists deeds only vindicate never purchase or obligate.",
  "material_contradiction": "none",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores share the forensic category of God declaring right standing against a charge (opposite of condemnation) for the sinner by grace through Christ. The book preserves that referent while materially altering precision, conditions, and extension: it foregrounds the broad lexical sense, re-describes the divine act as forgiveness rather than positive renaming/imputation of righteousness, and folds James-style vindication by deeds into the core definition instead of treating it as a harmonization problem.
